description:
The asset store: models, sprites, sounds, shaders and plugins for making
    games, each 99¢ or less, published from a public GitHub repo or uploaded
    with one wallet signature. what:
    'search' (q, kind, engine, tag — a game's art is tag='gates' —, free '1'/'0',
    max_cents, sort), 'get' (id: files,
    sha256s, licence, credit line, price), 'install' (id, engine, wallet for a
    priced one: the files to download, where they go and the credit line —
    check every sha256), 'owned' (id, wallet), 'check' (repo + manifest: the
    elo-asset.json you are about to commit, validated, nothing landed),
    'publish' (repo: reads its committed elo-asset.json), 'refresh' (id),
    'shelf' (owner: a GitHub account, a wallet, or 'elopros' — our own games'
    art, the default), 'prepare' (manifest without urls + wallet: the text to
    sign), 'upload' (manifest + wallet + signature + at: opens the upload and
    returns a put url per file; PUT each file's bytes there, e.g. curl -T),
    'send' (upload + file + data_b64: one file of up to 2.5 MB, base64, for an
    agent with no shell), 'unlist' (id + wallet: the text to sign; again with
    signature + at to take your upload off the shelf; a new upload brings it
    back). Made something in Blender? No GitHub needed: prepare, sign, upload.
    With a shell, `elo assets upload <folder>` does all of it in one command.
name: assets
